questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

He took a hurried glance / on the newspaper / and swiftly left for work.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'on the newspaper.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in 'on the newspaper' part of the sentence.
 
• **Use of On:** To indicate touching and being supported by the top surface of (something), or moving to a position that is supported by something.
 
 
• *Example: The book is lying on the table.*
 
 
 
• *​***Use of At**: to introduce prepositional phrases that identify the object of a sentence.
 
 
• *Example: He was looking at all the different options. *
 
 
 
• Therefore, the use of 'on the newspaper' should be replaced with 'at the newspaper' to make it grammatically correct.

 

Correct sentence__: *He took a hurried glance __at the newspaper__ and swiftly left for work.*

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The officers kept us waiting for one hour.

options.text: We were kept waiting for one hour by the officers.
We kept waiting for one hour.
We keep waiting for one hour.
We are keeping waiting for one hour.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'We were kept waiting for one hour by the officers.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in Simple past tense and in Active Voice.
 
• The rule for changing a sentence in Simple past Tense from active voice to passive voice:
 
 
• Interchange the object and subject with each other, i.e., the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The passive voice starts with the object of the active voice.
 
• Convert the verb into 3rd form of the verb.
 
• Structure: Subject + V2 + object (Active Voice)__
 
 

 Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject __(Passive Voice)__ 

__
 
• Solution: **He played football***. *(Active Voice)

 * Football was played by him**. *(Passive Voice)

 
• Therefore, the correct answer is 'We were kept waiting for one hour by the officers.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject performing an action.
 
• In Passive Voice, the sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
 
 
• Example: *He reads a novel. *(Active Voice)

 *A novel is read by him. *(Passive Voice)

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

My granny says that / it is quite right / to get married young, / though I do not absolute agree with her a bit on this.

options.text: though I do not absolute agree with her a bit on this

questions.solution:
The correct answer will be **"though I do not absolute agree with her a bit on this"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is divided into four parts. Among them one part is incorrect.
 
• In the last part, "**agree"** is a **verb**. Because of this, "**absolute"** will be an adverb before "**agree"**.
 
• **Adverbs** are used to provide additional details about a verb.
 
• We should use **"absolutely" **before "agree" that the sentence will be correct.

The correct sentence is **"My granny says that it is quite right to get married young, though I do not absolutely agree with her a bit on this."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The other parts of the given sentence are **grammatically **correct.
 
• **Adverbs** function as modifiers for verbs, adjectives, and other adverbs in English grammar. Adverbs and **adverbial phrases** frequently serve the purpose of describing the how, when, and where of events.
 
• If We do question how i agree, we will get answer **"absolutely"** as because this is used before verb **"agree"**.
